tierReasoning: Auth gate on an irreversible action (threadline_delete) extended to the DEFAULT MCP transport, plus a new loopback route. Auth + irreversibility = Tier 2 even though it ships dark.

scope.summary: SEC-018 stdio companion: one server-side performApprovedDelete (existence-check + enabled + revision-validated single-use consume + server-composed card + the irreversible mutation) that BOTH MCP transports invoke — HTTP in-process, stdio over the loopback POST /threadline/approved-delete route (agent-token + extracted evaluateLoopbackGuard; redeem-only; no caller-facing register/clear/consume/enabled). The delete handler holds no gate logic and does no local remove; a stdio transport failure is outcome-unknown, never a local delete. Dark default = byte-identical when the server is reachable.

evidence.incident: SEC-018b (#3218) gated threadline_delete only on the opt-in HTTP MCP transport; the DEFAULT per-session stdio helper (threadline.mcpHttp.enabled default false) ran in a separate process and was ungated — flipping the switch would protect only opt-in agents.
evidence.focusedTests: tests/unit/perform-approved-delete.test.ts (6, incl. hostile-caller no-mutation), tests/unit/approved-delete-loopback-guard.test.ts (4, tunnel-refusal), tests/unit/approved-delete-via-http.test.ts (5, outcome-unknown), tests/integration/owner-approved-action-stdio-transport.test.ts (hostile caller + positive control + dark + tunnel-refused), tests/e2e/owner-approved-action-stdio-transport-alive.test.ts (route alive + guard)
evidence.signalVsAuthority: isLocal stays a signal; sole authority is the device-signed owner-presence approval. Gate is synchronous server-side (no async fail-open); the route cannot authenticate the calling process — safety rests on redeem-only + the off-machine device signature (CoS-ratified).
